title: Chronic Glaucoma: Pressure Monitoring and Drop Adherence

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with ocular hypertension or chronic open-angle glaucoma (COAG): intraocular pressure (IOP) threshold, monitoring intervals, first-line laser or generic prostaglandin analogue, switching, preservative-free drops, and adherence and technique, using NICE NG81.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG81 as extracted gives no drug doses, dose frequencies or numeric target IOP beyond the 24 mmHg threshold; follow product information.
No formal contraindication list was in the extract.
No Saudi ophthalmology guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Referral is advised if IOP is 24 mmHg or more on Goldmann-type applanation tonometry after repeat measures. For newly diagnosed ocular hypertension with IOP of 24 mmHg or more, and for newly diagnosed non-advanced COAG, 360-degree selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is offered first; a generic prostaglandin analogue is offered if SLT is declined, unsuitable or as add-on. If a generic prostaglandin analogue is not tolerated, the first choice is an alternative generic prostaglandin analogue, then a beta-blocker. Escalation is offered only to people with satisfactory adherence and eye drop technique, so technique is demonstrated and observed when drops are first prescribed.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer for diagnosis
actions: Refer when IOP is 24 mmHg or more after repeat measures, after the baseline tests.

clinicalManagement.title: First-line treatment
actions: Offer 360-degree SLT for ocular hypertension with IOP 24 mmHg or more or non-advanced COAG; generic prostaglandin analogue if SLT declined, unsuitable or as add-on.

clinicalManagement.title: Teach drop technique
actions: Demonstrate correct technique and observe the person using it; ask about adherence and side effects at each assessment.

clinicalManagement.title: Switch or add
actions: Alternative generic prostaglandin analogue, then beta-blocker, then carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, sympathomimetic or miotic; consider preservative-free drops for allergy or ocular surface disease.

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: Use NG81 monitoring tables: 1 to 4 months if IOP not controlled; 12 to 18 months for stable low-risk COAG.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG81 names generic prostaglandin analogues, beta-blockers, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, sympathomimetics, miotics and latanoprost-netarsudil, and preservative-free preparations, but the extract gives no doses or frequencies. Follow product information and the ophthalmology protocol. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
